subject: VM attestation packet — expedited handback for SOC2 audit
messages:
From: Eleanor Price <eleanor.price@nexa.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Security Ops <security-ops@nexa.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T08:05:00Z
Subject: Request: compact vulnerability evidence packet for SOC2 auditor

Hi Monica,

We have a SOC2 auditor request that came in this morning asking for a compact vulnerability management evidence packet covering the last 90 days. They need:
- latest authenticated network + application scan index (timestamps + tool used)
- a short statement of scan cadence and owners
- SLA/commitment for CVE remediation windows by severity tier
- an attestation PDF signed by your security owner that recent critical/high CVEs have remediation plans and timelines

Can Redwood produce a handheld packet (attachments + short attestation) by EOD today? Our audit window is tight. If you can’t make EOD, please let me know latest ETA and any blockers.

Thanks,
Eleanor
Eleanor Price
Security Program Manager, NexaBank

P.S. if it helps we can accept a zipped evidence packet plus a DocuSign attestation link.
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Eleanor Price <eleanor.price@nexa.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T10:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: compact vulnerability evidence packet for SOC2 auditor

Eleanor —

We can deliver an expedited packet today. Summary of what I’m attaching and what follows in this thread:

Attachments included (zipped on the Drive link):
- vm-scan-index-20261028.csv — chronological index of authenticated scans (static + container image checks) with tool versions (Tenable.sc 2026.3, Trivy 0.41)
- scan-sla-summary-2026Q3.xlsx — table of SLA response/mitigation commitments by severity tier
- cve-closure-attestation-20261029.pdf — signed attestation from Redwood Security (see signature page)

Immediate notes / short answers for auditor:
- Scan cadence: authenticated external/full-stack weekly for production-critical tiers; monthly for lower-criticality environments; container image scans on push to registry (Trivy).
- Ownership: Naomi Feldman (Security Ops) oversees scan scheduling and triage; Engineering owns fix timelines per SLA.
- SLA windows (high level): Critical — 7 calendar days to mitigation plan + 30 days to mitigation or documented compensating control; High — 14 days to plan + 60 days to mitigation; Medium/Low — standard quarterly backlog. See attached spreadsheet for exceptions/escrows.

Kimberly will add the signed attestation and clarify any compliance-specific wording. We’ve included a DocuSign link for the auditor to finalize acceptance if that is required.

Next steps:
- Kimberly: finalize attestation PDF and sign
- Naomi: confirm the CSV has the latest authenticated scan timestamps and add any pending remediation owners

Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Security Solutions — Redwood Inference

Eleanor / Monica —

I validated the scan index and added inline notes to the CSV where a remediation ticket is open. Quick clarifications for the auditor:

- Tools & scope: Tenable.sc scheduled authenticated scans for externally-exposed hosts and key internal stacks; Trivy for container image scanning and CVE detection in CI.
- Confirmation windows:
  * Critical CVEs (CVSS >= 9.0): automated detection -> triage within 24 hours -> mitigation plan by 7 days
  * High (7.0–8.9): triage within 72 hours -> mitigation plan by 14 days
  * We maintain a 30/60 exception process documented in the SLA spreadsheet for vendor/vendor-locked fixes.
- Evidence of closure: for each remediated critical/high CVE we include the remediation ticket URL and the final verification scan timestamp (see CSV notes column).

Eleanor: I’ve highlighted three critical CVEs that are in plan stage (ticket IDs included). If the auditor needs direct access to verification scans we can provision read-only access to a limited scan result folder — let me know.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Security Operations — Redwood Inference
